unit.why: A homiletic note on the word בהמה, quoted from a book, wraps a short anecdote from an old manuscript about a sage who sold his Zohar, was tormented in dreams, and returned it.

stories.start_quote: דחכם אחד היה לו ס׳ הזהר ומכרו
stories.end_quote: הלך והחזיר הזהר ע״כ כתוב בס׳ הנז'
stories.summary_en: A sage sold his copy of the Zohar. At night he was tormented and called 'beast' (בהמה). A scholar explained that the word is an acronym for 'you have removed the holy from the house', so the sage went and took the Zohar back.

tags.why: The anecdote is embedded in a homiletic explanation of why a sinner is called בהמה.

quotes: ובלילה היו מצערין אותו וקורין אותו בהמה
tags.why: The night-time dream reproach drives the plot.
